description: Manually curated STRIDE ground truth for the Cloud Data Ingest Pipeline. Each threat is keyed by its target (component_id or data_flow_id) plus STRIDE category; that (target, category) pair is the intended matching key for evaluation. This architecture is deliberately built so that all data flows are well-secured (authenticated + encrypted) and the real risk lives in per-component configuration/posture (the `config` field): a publicly readable, unencrypted bucket; an over-privileged processing role; a warehouse without encryption or audit logging; disabled rate limiting; and effectively disabled monitoring. Such threats are marked `hard` because they require security knowledge and configuration reasoning rather than a single boolean attribute, and the deterministic baseline (which ignores `config`) cannot find them.

threats.description: The internet-exposed ingest API can be targeted by producers impersonating legitimate partners.
threats.mitigation: Require signed requests or mutual TLS and validate producer identity on every call.

threats.description: The public ingest endpoint can receive malformed or malicious records (injection, schema abuse).
threats.mitigation: Validate and sanitize all incoming records against a strict schema before storage.

threats.description: Producers could deny submitting specific records if request provenance is not reliably recorded.
threats.mitigation: Record signed, timestamped provenance for each ingested record.

threats.description: Rate limiting is disabled (config.rate_limiting_enabled = false), so a producer can flood the pipeline and exhaust downstream capacity.
threats.mitigation: Enable rate limiting and per-producer quotas at the ingest edge.

threats.description: The raw bucket is publicly readable and unencrypted at rest (config.public_access = true, encryption_at_rest = false), directly exposing sensitive raw records to anyone on the internet.
threats.mitigation: Disable public access, enforce bucket policies/Block Public Access, and enable encryption at rest.

threats.description: Public access combined with disabled versioning (config.versioning_enabled = false) lets an attacker overwrite or delete raw objects with no recovery path.
threats.mitigation: Restrict write access, enable versioning, and use object lock for immutability.

threats.description: Access logging is disabled (config.access_logging_enabled = false), so reads and writes to sensitive raw data cannot be attributed.
threats.mitigation: Enable server access logging / data-event logging and ship logs to a protected store.

threats.description: The processing cluster runs with an account-wide admin role (config.iam_role = admin, iam_role_scope = account-wide); a single compromised job can take over the whole account.
threats.mitigation: Apply least-privilege IAM scoped to required resources and use per-job roles.

threats.description: IMDSv1 is allowed (config.instance_metadata_v2_required = false), enabling SSRF-based theft of the cluster's powerful role credentials.
threats.mitigation: Require IMDSv2 (hop limit 1) and block SSRF paths to the metadata endpoint.

threats.description: The warehouse stores sensitive processed data without encryption at rest (config.encryption_at_rest = false), exposing it via snapshots, backups, or disk access.
threats.mitigation: Enable encryption at rest with managed keys and restrict snapshot sharing.

threats.description: Audit logging is disabled (config.audit_logging_enabled = false), so queries against and changes to sensitive data cannot be attributed.
threats.mitigation: Enable audit/connection logging and forward it to tamper-evident storage.

threats.description: Sensitive processed records could be modified without authorization if warehouse access controls are weak.
threats.mitigation: Enforce least-privilege database roles and monitor write/DDL activity.

threats.description: Log retention is zero and alerting is disabled (config.log_retention_days = 0, alerting_enabled = false), so security-relevant events are neither retained nor noticed, undermining attribution across the whole pipeline.
threats.mitigation: Set an adequate retention period, protect logs from deletion, and enable alerting.
